title: Check: The Lowest and Highest Subnets

questions.prompt: Why did the old rules skip the lowest subnet (subnet zero)?
options: Its network address is identical to the network address of the whole network, so mask-less routing protocols couldn't tell them apart

questions.prompt: Why did the old rules skip the highest subnet (the all-ones subnet)?
options: Its hosts can't reach the internet
It's too small to be useful
Its broadcast address matches the broadcast address of the whole network

questions.prompt: Under the old rule, how many usable subnets do you get by borrowing 3 bits?
Under modern rules (RFC 1878), how many subnets do you get by borrowing 3 bits?
Under the old rule, splitting a /24 into two /25s gave you no usable subnets at all.
What made subnet zero safe to use?
options: Routing protocols that carry the mask with every route, like RIPv2, OSPF, and BGP

questions.prompt: Since subnet zero is allowed now, the network and broadcast addresses inside each subnet can also be given to hosts.
Which classful routing protocol, version 1 of a well-known one, didn't send masks? (acronym)
